title: Finite product compactification geometry and canonical maps
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and write $D(S)=D(S_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for ordinary unbounded derived constant-module sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the K-flat derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor], derived pullback and direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], extension by zero for open immersions [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and the signed tensor symmetry $\sigma$ [def-pur-finite-forward-tensor-symmetry]. For scheme maps $f:X\to B$ and $g:Z\to B$, choose compactifications $X\xrightarrow{j}\bar X\xrightarrow{a}B$ and $Z\xrightarrow{k}\bar Z\xrightarrow{b}B$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. A product geometry consists of these compactifications and three Cartesian cones [def-pc-fibre-product]: $P=X\times_B Z$ with projections $p,q$, $W=X\times_B\bar Z$ with projections $s,v$, and $T=\bar X\times_B\bar Z$ with projections $r,t$. The canonical product geometry uses the actual chosen fibre products. Let $u_1:P\to W$ be the Cartesian lift of $(p,kq)$ and $u_2:W\to T$ the Cartesian lift of $(js,v)$. Their defining projection equations give Cartesian open squares with $k$ and $j$, respectively. Put $u=u_2u_1$ and $c=bt$; the product compactification of $h=gq$ is $P\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{c}B$.

For $M\in D(X)$ and $N\in D(Z)$ define $D=Lp^*M\otimes^L Lq^*N$ and $E=Lr^*j_!M\otimes^L Lt^*k_!N$. The following auxiliary maps always mean the canonical constructions: tensoring an arrow in either variable; applying open extension to an arrow; the pullback comparison $La^*Lb^*\cong Ld^*$ induced by $ba=d$; the open-extension compositor $b_!a_!\cong(ba)_!$; and open base change $Lb^*j_!\cong j'_!La^*$ for a Cartesian open square $(a,j',j,b)$. Write $\gamma_j:j_!K\otimes^L L\to j_!(K\otimes^L Lj^*L)$ for the inverse open projection isomorphism of [def-exchange-projection]. In such a square the left open tensor step is open base change on the first factor followed by $\gamma_{j'}$. The right open tensor step is open base change on the second factor, $\sigma$ moving its open extension to the left, $\gamma_{j'}$, and $j'_!(\sigma)$ restoring the order. When one factor is pulled back along a commuting triangle, append the corresponding pullback comparison inside $j'_!$. Apply the right step to $u_1$ to obtain
$$e_{\mathrm{in}}:Ls^*M\otimes^L Lv^*k_!N\longrightarrow (u_1)_!D,$$
and the left step to $u_2$ to obtain
$$e_{\mathrm{out}}:E\longrightarrow (u_2)_!(Ls^*M\otimes^L Lv^*k_!N).$$
Define the specified open tensor map $e:E\to u_!D$ as $e_{\mathrm{out}}$, then $(u_2)_!(e_{\mathrm{in}})$, then the canonical open-extension compositor. This defines the map, without asserting any comparison theorem about it.

For any displayed compactification $d$ of a map $z$, write $F_z^d=R(d_{\mathrm{proper}})_*(d_{\mathrm{open}})_!$. For composable compactifiable quasi-compact maps $z,y$, displayed compactifications $d_z,d_y,d_{yz}$, and an object $K$ in the bounded-below etale-origin class [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], define $\alpha_{z,y}:F_y^{d_y}F_z^{d_z}K\to F_{yz}^{d_{yz}}K$ by first transporting the inner and outer compactifications to the globally chosen ones using the normalized comparisons [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], realized on the etale-origin class by the canonical candidate comparison [def-sf-origin-candidate-comparison], applying the canonical origin compositor [thm-sf-comp-composition], and transporting the output to $d_{yz}$. For original compactifications $c_f,c_g$ (independent of the displayed product geometry), set $F=F_f^{c_f}M$, $G=F_g^{c_g}N$ and $c_q=c_f$ base-changed along $g$. For $f,g$ quasi-compact and compactifiable, a compactification $c_h$ of $h$, and $D$ in the etale-origin class, define the chosen forward product $\Xi_{f,g}:F\otimes^L G\to F_h^{c_h}D$ by the exact word
$$\alpha_{q,g}\circ F_g^{c_g}(\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lp^*M,N})\circ F_g^{c_g}(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}\otimes1_N)\circ F_g^{c_g}(\sigma_{N,Lg^*F})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G},$$
where the projection and compact-support exchange maps are the canonical maps of [def-exchange-projection], with $q$ represented by $c_q$.

Finally define the product tensor-domain predicate to mean that all six objects
$$F\otimes^L G,\quad G\otimes^L F,\quad N\otimes^L Lg^*F,\quad Lg^*F\otimes^L N,\quad F_q^{c_q}(Lp^*M)\otimes^L N,\quad D$$
belong to the bounded-below etale-origin class on $B,B,Z,Z,Z,P$, respectively. The preceding geometry, objects, canonical auxiliary maps, open tensor map, normalized displayed-coordinate compositor, forward word, and domain predicate are definitions; no binary compactification comparison equality is part of this definition.
